messages:
harini: Hey team, seeing a spike of CI failures starting ~01:12 UTC. GitLab runners fail during OIDC exchange with STS — immediate 401s. Error in our logs: "token validation failed: subject claim truncated or invalid length". Repro attempt attached.

samir: Ugh. Any sample logs or the exact error string? Is this across all runners or a single project?

harini: It's ~20 jobs across 5 projects (mostly monorepo pipelines). Paste of the runner log:```2026-03-15T01:12:06Z runner[pid=4221] ERROR exchange_for_token: http 401 {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"subject claim length 96 > max 64"}```

elaine: That "> max 64" rings a bell — we tightened subject length validation in the STS authorization check earlier this quarter. Could the GitLab OIDC sub include long paths?

kevin: GitLab runner OIDC sub format changed for group namespaces a while back, includes full path: `project:group/subgroup/repo:ref` which can be >64 chars for deep orgs. Can you pull the raw JWT from one of the failed runners?

harini: Yes. From a failing runner I grabbed the token exchange request and decoded the payload with `jwt -d`. Payload snippet:```{
  "iss": "https://gitlab.com",
  "sub": "project:acme/eng/platform/release-candidates/long-branch-name",
  "aud": ["https://sts.internal.redwood"],
  "exp": 1710234726
}```

ci-deploy-bot: automated note: impacted jobs count = 19, queued = 3, backoff triggered. :warning:

samir: That sub is clearly >64 chars. STS validator expects our internal service-account-sub to be <=64 because older service accounts use `sa:<id>` format. The new GitLab format breaks the check.

elaine: Two problems then: 1) validation now rejects valid upstream tokens (breaking CI), 2) our least-priv checks use subject parsing to map to service account impersonation. We need a short-term fix to restore CI and a long-term policy.

kevin: Short term options: relax subject-length check to 256 chars OR normalize subs by hashing/truncating before validation (but that affects mapping). Which is safest for tonight?

harini: User impact is high. Recommend relaxing length limit to 256 to triage, add an alert for mapping failures. I'll open a rollback if anyone objects.

samir: +1 for minimal change. Also add an ingress check that logs full sub and project to help map to SA later.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: change `sts-validator.max_sub_len` 64->256 on canary (2 pods) in prod, roll 10% -> 50% -> 100%. CI-critical label attached.

harini: Rolling to canary now. Will watch job queue.

(5m pass)

harini: Canary applied, two pods with new config. Queued jobs started succeeding. Replayed 5 failed runs, all passed token exchange step.

elaine: Good. For long-term: we should stop relying on raw `sub` string to resolve service-account mapping. Proposal: support an explicit OIDC claim (eg. `redwood_sa`) or use `sub`->`lookup` table where we map common GitLab subject patterns to SAs. Also add a fallback hash-based mapping and store mapping metadata in our config DB.

kevin: Agreed. Also two follow-ups: 1) increase default token lifetime acceptance window to tolerate short TTL skew from runners (we saw one job with exp ttl only 12s left), 2) document recommended GitLab runner config: set `oidc_sub_format: short` if available or add canonical project id claim.

samir: Draft change for mapping logic (pseudo):```- if payload.redwood_sa present -> use that- else if sub matches /^project:[^:]+/ -> lookup pattern -> resolve SA id- else -> compute sha256(sub) as fallback key and check mapping table```

harini: I'll create a support KB and send recommended GitLab runner settings to customers impacted. For the internal change, please add a post-deploy test that runs a GitLab sample job and does end-to-end impersonation.

infra-bot: prod roll to 100% completed at 01:32 UTC. All canaries healthy.

ci-deploy-bot: automated note: retried 19 failed jobs, 18 succeeded, 1 still in pending due to unrelated runner capacity.

kevin: We've captured a list of example subs to seed the mapping table. I'll follow up with the patch to the mapping service and an RFC for `redwood_sa` claim support.

elaine: Action items: harini -> KB + customer outreach. kevin -> RFC & mapping patch. samir -> monitor for mapping failures and add alert. I'll open infra task to remove the temporary 256 limit once mapping is live to avoid unbounded subs.

harini: Thanks all. Marking incident as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:
